title: Decouple ProgramLabelResolver from Flutter/Riverpod so its label logic can be unit-tested without pumpWidget

evidence.quote: /// Layering: pure Dart domain layer — no Flutter, Riverpod, Drift, or Firebase.

why: ProgramLabelResolver sits in domain/labels/ next to projection/, whose own docstring declares the module 'pure Dart domain layer — no Flutter, Riverpod, Drift, or Firebase' — but this file imports flutter/widgets.dart and flutter_riverpod directly, and its only public constructors take a WidgetRef or a Riverpod Ref (the plain constructor is private). The label-selection methods themselves (learningProgramLabel, calendarEntryLabel, calendarEntryTodayRef) only need a DomainTermLabels value and, for one method, an AppLocalizations instance — none of that requires Flutter widgets. Because the constructor is gated behind Ref, every one of program_label_resolver_test.dart's ~13 cases is forced into testWidgets + pumpWidget(ProviderScope(MaterialApp(Scaffold(Consumer(...))))) + pumpAndSettle, for what is fundamentally a handful of ternary/fallback string picks — a real, measured cost in test complexity and runtime versus a plain test().
recommendation: Expose a public ProgramLabelResolver(DomainTermLabels labels) constructor (or move the file to presentation/) so the label logic is unit-testable directly; keep .of(ref)/.fromRef(ref) as thin wiring factories.
acceptance_criteria: ProgramLabelResolver has a public constructor independent of WidgetRef/Ref.
The majority of program_label_resolver_test.dart's cases are converted to plain test() cases against the new constructor; only the .of(ref)/.fromRef(ref) wiring keeps a thin widget/provider test.
